transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-01-28 15:00 PST
Duration: 46 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Miguel (Redwood), Michael (Orion CTO), Sarah (Orion ML), Darius (Orion Security), Lena (Orion PM)

Summary:
Quick weekly POC sync to review the latest model comparison results, decide on pinning policy for pilot traffic, and agree on rollback/fallback behavior for production-like tests. Emphasis on latency vs cost tradeoffs and security constraints (VPC/KMS).

Topics covered (auto tags): model selection, version pinning, fallback policies, canary rollouts, quantization, latency heatmap, security/KMS, prompt set alignment.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll do a quick rundwon — uh rundown of the model results we sent yesterday and then get into pin strategy. michelle? michael? you there?
[00:15] Michael (Orion): yeah yep, on my end. thanks Alex. we skimmed the spreadsheet, big picture — latency a little higher than we expected on the larger models.
[00:34] Priya (Redwood SE): yeah so just to call out, the numbers are median p50 p95 across the prompt set you sent, we ran on Redwood Dedicated equivalent hardware. quantized runs were also included, but note quantized latency for decoding is a hair different when your sequence lengths vary.
[00:57] Sarah (Orion): quick clarifying q: when you say quantized, is that int8 per layer or some hybrid approach? sometimes the names in the sheet differ.
[01:12] Priya: we used dynamic int8 for the bulk and mixed per-op on attention kernels; the sheet labels it "dyn-int8 (mixed-kern)" — apologies if that was confusing, and the runtime logging shows kernel-level fallbacks when sequence grows.
[01:37] Darius (Orion Security): I just want to flag KMS and audit logs — the POC needs key usage traces plus retention policy, and any pinning decision mustn't break our separation of logs between prod and pilot.
[01:55] Alex: totally agreed — Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and audit logs; we'll attach the SOC 2 appendix. i'll follow up with the exact audit log fields.
[02:10] Lena (PM): what we want from this call is 1) pick a model family for the pilot, 2) decide if we pin to exact model version or allow soft-fallbacks, and 3) understand rollback behavior.
[02:32] Priya: i recommend a two-tier pin policy: canonical pin to a model family + strong pin to a specific version for the production pilot run. soft fallback policy would permit routing to a quantized variant of the same family when capacity or latency SLOs are breached.
[02:50] Michael: explain the difference for us in practice — what happens if p95 latency spikes?
[02:59] Priya: if p95 > target for two consecutive 5m windows, the routing layer can shift x% of traffic to a lower-latency variant. we suggest an initial canary of 10% traffic for 30 minutes, then evaluate quality metrics (rouge/bleu not perfect for your prompts so we'll use your labelled failure rate).
[03:24] Sarah: labeled failure rate — that we can calculate on your side if we give the set. but we also need to agree what counts as failure — hallucination vs timeout vs factual mismatch.
[03:38] Alex: yes let's codify. Sarah, can you send the three canonical failure examples you mentioned in the sheet?
[03:45] Sarah: i'll add them.
[03:50] [05:01] Miguel (Redwood): i want to add a note about model catalog naming — in the sheet we showed family names and build numbers, but some tooling reads compatibility differently. if you pin to family:family-v2 we need to ensure the runtime mapping to a quantized fallback is explicit, otherwise the soft fallback may pick a different architecture.
[05:27] Michael: are there situations where fallback could be to a completely different model (e.g., smaller architecture) that changes output distribution? that's a big product risk.
[05:42] Priya: yes, it can, which is why we recommend a policy that only allows fallbacks within the same family or a verified behavior-matched variant. Redwood Console includes a compatibility score — we can share thresholds so you can veto fallbacks that exceed X% divergence.
[06:05] Darius: also, from security side, if fallback is served from a different cluster or region, we need to make sure data residency rules apply — are we able to restrict fallback to same VPC?
[06:20] Alex: we can restrict by policy; Redwood Private and Dedicated allow routing constraints by region/VPC. soft fallback can be constrained to the same VPC or marked as disallowed.
[06:36] [09:10] Lena: cost perspective — smaller models are cheaper but sometimes quality drops. what's the recommended approach for the pilot when cost vs quality is an explicit success metric?
[09:27] Priya: run a blended metric: cost-per-successful-inference. we'll provide per-prompt token cost and a delta quality score. for pilot, we recommend prioritizing quality (you flagged user-visible correctness) while measuring cost; after week 2 we can tune thresholds.
[09:48] Michael: i noticed on the sheet the medium model had much lower p95 but slightly higher failure rate for fraud-detection prompts. is that expected?
[10:05] Priya: yes some models trade off calibration for latency. for fraud prompts where exact numeric extraction matters, certain decoder configs perform better. we can test adjusted sampling/temperature to reduce those failures without switching model family.
[10:27] Sarah: can you run a sweep with top-p 0.9, temperature 0.2 and then a deterministic sampling for extraction tasks?
[10:39] Priya: yes we'll add that to the next run and include paramized results.
[10:46] [12:00] Miguel: operationally for pinning, there's two levers — pin-by-route (per-endpoint) or pin-global (account-level). most customers want route-level pins for gradual rollouts.
[12:18] Michael: we'll need route-level granularity, different teams use different routes.
[12:24] Alex: ok route-level pin it is. note also you can have a fallback policy on the route that overrides account defaults.
[12:32] Darius: on rollback — what's the simplest safe rollback?
[12:38] Priya: a safe rollback is instantaneous mapping to the previous pinned version with a short canary to confirm metrics; we recommend an automated scoreboard that checks latency and your labeled failure rate before completing rollback.
[12:52] Lena: what's the human workflow for rollback? i.e., does someone from our side need to approve?
[12:58] Alex: by default we can configure auto-rollback with preapproved thresholds, otherwise manual button in Redwood Console requiring two approvers.
[13:10] [15:00] Michael: curious about the "compatibility score" — how's that computed?
[15:07] Priya: it's a combination of embedding distance on your prompt set, behavioral regression checks on typical outputs, and a light eval suite. it's not perfect but it helps filter wild fallbacks.
[15:22] Michael: can we see the compatibility numbers for the three candidate models?
[15:29] Alex: yes, included in spreadsheet — we'll highlight them in the version with per-prompt breakdown.
[15:36] Sarah: small note — we saw a few transcription typos in the sheet where "kv cache" was written as "kay vee cash" in the notes, so just want the raw logs for debugging.
[15:48] Priya: haha noted, sorry for the run-on notes. we'll send the runtime traces (k-v cache entries and token-level timings).
[16:05] [18:00] Miguel: about bench infra — we ran everything in a closed box with fixed concurrency. your real traffic will vary; for the pilot we suggest a shadowed A/B where 5% of production traffic is mirrored to Redwood Dedicated to validate latency under real variance but not serve responses to users.
[18:23] Michael: shadowing sounds good. what's the overhead?
[18:29] Priya: negligible on your prod side; it's just a copy. costwise we bill for the mirrored requests but that's fine for a pilot.
[18:40] Darius: must ensure mirrored data is obfuscated for PCI fields — we cannot send clear PANs in the payload.
[18:49] Alex: agreed, we'll add a preprocessing step to mask sensitive fields and confirm on your PII rules.
[19:03] [21:00] Lena: ok decision time — which model family are we leaning to? any objections to family-X for the pilot?
[21:12] Michael: family-X seems reasonable if the p95 is within target after the quantized tweak. my caveat is we want strict same-family fallback only.
[21:25] Priya: we can implement same-family-only policy. initial pin: family-X v2.1 for route /payments/extract, with a soft fallback to family-X v2.1-quant (quantized variant).
[21:40] Sarah: for routes doing sensitive extraction we'll keep a strong pin to the exact version for two weeks to collect metrics.
[21:50] Alex: so to confirm: route-level pin to family-X v2.1, soft fallback allowed only to family-X quant variant, auto-canary 10% for 30m, and strong-pin windows for sensitive routes. correct?
[22:04] Michael: yes.
[22:08] [25:00] Priya: i'll draft the pin policy doc and include YAML examples for Redwood Console and API — you'll be able to set canary windows, thresholds, and VPC constraints.
[25:20] Lena: can you also include a sample rollback runbook for the on-call team? because we don't want to have to escalate to Redwood SEs for simple rollbacks.
[25:32] Miguel: we'll include the runbook and a button in the console. two-click rollback flow.
[25:41] Darius: please include a section on KMS key rotation and proof of deletion for pilot data.
[25:49] Alex: adding that.
[26:10] [29:00] Sarah: on evaluation, besides labelled failure rate, can we run a small human eval for the top 200 responses after week 1?
[29:18] Priya: yes Redwood can run a human-in-the-loop sample review and provide a dashboard with triage tags.
[29:28] Michael: cost estimate for the pilot for shadowing + 5% production?
[29:35] Alex: we'll send a detailed cost estimate; rough ballpark is X tokens cost + reserved capacity for the dedicated nodes; included in the spreadsheet follow-up.
[29:50] [32:00] Lena: timeline check: we want to start production-like shadowing by Feb 12. is that feasible?
[32:09] Priya: yes assuming we get your prompt set and the security checklist answered by Feb 5, we can schedule infra and run the shadow test on Feb 12.
[32:22] Michael: ok that aligns with our internal release window.
[32:29] [35:00] Miguel: small gotcha: the runtime will auto select different kernels for long sequences, that sometimes increases variance. we'll add kernel-locked runs for consistency tests.
[35:15] Sarah: useful — include both kernel-locked and standard runs in the next sheet.
[35:23] Priya: will do.
[35:30] [38:00] Alex: recap and next steps — Alex to send model perf sheet with per-prompt latencies (by 01-30); Priya to send pin policy draft + YAML examples (by 02-04); Orion to supply canonical prompt set and failure examples (by 02-03); schedule VPC deep dive week of Feb 10.
[38:22] Lena: any other blocking items?
[38:27] Darius: none from security besides the KMS items already noted.
[38:33] Michael: no blockers.
[38:36] [41:00] Alex: alright thanks everyone. we'll follow up in email with the files and set up the VPC meeting.
[41:09] Sarah: thanks all.
[41:12] Miguel: thanks.
[41:15] [45:30] (call ends)

Post-call notes:
- Redwood to highlight compatibility scores and per-prompt deltas in the follow-up sheet.
- Agreed pilot config: route-level pin to family-X v2.1 with quantized same-family soft fallback; strong pin windows on sensitive extraction routes; 10% canary for 30m before full shift.
- Security follow-ups: KMS, masking for shadow traffic, audit log fields.
